Stated Claim / Post Context:
NYC teacher posts antisemitic meme of Lionel Messi

A New York City Schools teacher has been posting antisemitic memes on social media, including pictures that disturbingly echo Nazi propaganda.

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

Her goal is hate.

A New York City public schools teacher has been posting antisemitic memes on social media, including grotesque caricatures of Argentina soccer star Lionel Messi that echo Nazi propaganda depicting Jews as greedy and scheming.

Park Slope Collegiate math teacher Maysa Jarara posted an image July 19 on Facebook under the name Maysa, showing a crying, groveling Messi with a super-sized nose, wearing a yarmulke as he rubs his hands together.

“The look on his face is priceless,” Jarara captioned the photo, which resembles a despicable  antisemitic internet meme called “The Happy Merchant.”

Messi, who visited Israel as part of a “peace tour” in 2013, was the subject of antisemitic conspiracy theories during the World Cup, claiming that Jews control Fédération Internationale de Football Association, soccer’s regulatory body, and have worked behind the scenes to benefit his career, according to online antisemitism watchdog nonprofit Cyberwell.

“Jarara has crossed a major line by trafficking in classic antisemitic tropes that cast Jews as greedy and scheming,” United Jewish Teachers President Moshe Spern said.

The Brooklyn math teacher also regularly reposts messages denigrating Israel, including one featuring the Israeli flag covered in blood.

On the three-year anniversary of Hamas’ barbaric Oct. 7, 2023 attacks, which killed over 1,200 Israelis, Jarara posted an illustration to Instagram of a keffiyeh-clad man dancing with a woman in a hijab in front of a burning pile. “And we love life and we can live it in a way,” reads the caption.

“This is deeply disturbing. We have a teacher who is entrusted with educating children publicly sharing inflammatory, biased, and historically misleading posts about Israel and the Jewish people,” New York City Public Schools Alliance President Karen Feldman said.

DOE schools have been plagued with antisemitism since the October 7 attacks, with numerous teachers being caught engaging in Jew hatred online.

Damian Neva, who teaches history at P.S. 77 in Park Slope texted in a groupchat “Long live Yahya Al-Sinwar,” to other terrorism lovers looking to implement a boycott of Israeli goods at The Park Slope Food Co-op, according to a bombshell lawsuit.

Brooklyn social studies teacher at IS 181 George Trim was reprimanded by the DOE after he was caught hosting an antisemitic conspiracy podcast while clad in a literal tinfoil hat.

Thousands of NYC Jewish families have pulled their kids out of public schools to shield them from the nonstop anti-Israel brainwashing going on in city classrooms.

Jewish schools in the Big Apple and across the Empire State have seen a surge in enrollment, with a roughly 3,100 influx, according to a study from Teach Coalition.

Jarara, who earned $140,000 in 2025 according to public records, could not be reached for comment.
